seo.description: Developers, JSM & Jira, design, and marketing — a full-cycle digital studio serving clients worldwide.

jira.q: Do you set up Jira from scratch or fix an existing project?
jira.a: Both. We can configure new Jira projects from zero, or audit and restructure an existing setup that has become slow or confusing to use.

jira.q: Can you customize workflows for our specific processes?
jira.a: Yes — we build custom statuses, transitions, and automation rules that match how your team actually works, whether that's Scrum, Kanban, or a hybrid process.

jira.q: Do you set up reporting and dashboards?
jira.a: Yes. We configure dashboards and reports (velocity, burndown, cycle time) so leads and stakeholders can see progress without asking for manual updates.

jira.q: Can Jira integrate with our other tools?
jira.a: Yes — we connect Jira with Slack, Bitbucket/GitHub, Confluence, and other tools so updates and notifications flow automatically.
We include onboarding sessions and documentation as part of every setup, ensuring your team adopts the new structure quickly and consistently.

slack.q: Can you clean up a messy Slack workspace?
slack.a: Yes — we audit existing channels, archive unused ones, and restructure the workspace around teams and projects so it is easy to navigate again.

slack.q: Can you build custom Slack bots?
slack.a: Yes. We build bots and workflows for common requests — standup reminders, ticket updates, approval flows — using Slack's native Workflow Builder or custom integrations.

slack.q: Can Slack notify us automatically from Jira or ClickUp?
slack.a: Yes — we set up two-way integrations so status changes, comments, and mentions in Jira/ClickUp post directly into the appropriate Slack channels.

slack.q: How do you prevent notification overload?
slack.a: We configure notification rules and channel defaults so team members are only pinged for what is relevant to them — reducing noise and speeding up responses.

slack.q: How long does a Slack setup take?
slack.a: A typical workspace restructuring and integration setup takes about 1 week, depending on team size and the number of connected tools.

figma.q: Do you design from scratch or work with an existing brand?
figma.a: Both. We can create a new visual direction from scratch, or design within your existing brand guidelines and design system.

figma.q: What do I receive at handover — just images or developer-ready assets?
figma.a: Developers receive a fully organized Figma file with components, auto-layout, and Dev Mode inspection — allowing them to extract exact spacing, colors, and assets directly.

figma.q: Can you build an interactive prototype I can test with users?
figma.a: Yes — we build clickable prototypes that simulate real navigation and interactions, enabling you to test the user flow before a single line of code is written.

figma.q: Do you design for both web and mobile?
figma.a: Yes — we design responsive web interfaces and native-feeling mobile app screens, maintaining a unified design system for consistency.

figma.q: How long does a design project take?
figma.a: A typical project — from wireframes through to final UI — takes 2–5 weeks depending on the screen count and feedback iterations.

photoshop.q: What kind of images do you edit?
photoshop.a: Product photos, portraits, marketing banners, social media graphics, and composite images — anything requiring retouching, color correction, or manipulation.

photoshop.q: Can you align our social media graphics with our existing brand?
photoshop.a: Yes — we work from your brand colors, typography, and style guides (or help create them) so every graphic reflects a unified brand image.

photoshop.q: Do you handle photo compositing (combining multiple images)?
photoshop.a: Yes — ranging from simple background swaps to complex photorealistic composites blending several source images into a seamless visual.
Our standard process includes revision rounds until you are satisfied with the outcome — typical projects finalize within 2–3 feedback cycles.

photoshop.q: How fast can you deliver a batch of images?
photoshop.a: A standard batch (10–20 images) is usually delivered within 3–5 business days, depending on technical complexity.

illustrator.q: What is included in a logo design project?
illustrator.a: A complete brand mark with logo variations (horizontal, icon-only, monochrome), vector source files (SVG, AI, EPS), and a brand book covering color palettes, typography, and usage guidelines.

illustrator.q: Can you design a custom icon set for our product or app?
illustrator.a: Yes — we craft cohesive icon sets matching your brand identity, delivered as scalable vector assets ready for web or mobile implementation.

illustrator.q: Do you prepare files for print as well as digital use?
illustrator.a: Yes — we prepare print-ready files configured with accurate color profiles (CMYK), bleed areas, and resolutions for business cards, packaging, banners, and merchandise.

illustrator.q: Will vector graphics maintain sharpness at any scale?
illustrator.a: Yes — everything is built in vector format, allowing logos and icons to scale seamlessly from a small favicon up to a billboard without quality loss.

illustrator.q: How long does a logo or icon set project take?
illustrator.a: A logo design project typically takes 1–2 weeks including revisions; a full icon set usually follows a similar timeline depending on quantity.

premiere.q: What types of video content do you edit?
premiere.a: Promotional videos, product demos, social media clips, testimonials, and brand videos — from raw footage assembly to a polished final cut.

premiere.q: Do you handle color grading and audio cleanup?
premiere.a: Yes — every project includes color grading for visual consistency and audio processing (noise reduction, leveling) to ensure high-quality sound.

premiere.q: Can you add subtitles or closed captions?
premiere.a: Yes — we produce accurate subtitles in your required languages, styled for accessibility and optimized for muted social media playback.

premiere.q: Do you export platform-specific video formats?
premiere.a: Yes — we deliver assets tailored to specific channels (Instagram Reels, YouTube, LinkedIn, TikTok), using appropriate aspect ratios and compression specs.

premiere.q: What is the typical turnaround time for a video edit?
premiere.a: A standard short-form video (under 2 minutes) is usually delivered in 3–5 business days; complex or longer edits take a bit more time.

metaMarketing.q: Do you handle both campaign strategy and ad creatives?
metaMarketing.a: Yes — we develop campaign strategy and audience targeting parameters, alongside designing creative assets (images, video, copy) to ensure unified execution.

metaMarketing.q: How do you measure ad campaign performance?
metaMarketing.a: We configure the Meta Pixel and conversion tracking events, then run continuous A/B tests on creative and audience parameters to optimize return on ad spend.

metaMarketing.q: What initial ad budget is required to start?
metaMarketing.a: We work with a range of budgets and will recommend an appropriate starting figure based on your target market and goals during a discovery call.

metaMarketing.q: Will I receive business-focused performance reports?
metaMarketing.a: Yes — we track core business metrics including Cost Per Lead (CPL), Cost Per Acquisition (CPA), ROAS, and conversion trends rather than vanity impressions.

metaMarketing.q: How long before we see performance results?
metaMarketing.a: Initial performance data is collected within 1–2 weeks; most campaigns reach optimized, predictable performance after approximately 4 weeks of testing.

seo.q: Do you begin with a technical SEO audit?
seo.a: Yes — we evaluate site performance, indexing health, mobile usability, and architecture to resolve technical issues suppressing your rankings first.

seo.q: How do you select target keywords?
seo.a: We conduct keyword research based on search intent, industry competition, and conversion potential to target audiences actively seeking your services.

seo.q: Do you handle content production or provide briefs?
seo.a: Both options are available — we can produce fully optimized content or supply detailed content briefs for your in-house team to write.

seo.q: Is sustainable link building included in the service?
seo.a: Yes — we execute white-hat link acquisition strategies to build domain authority while protecting your site against search engine penalties.

seo.q: When can we expect ranking improvements?
seo.a: SEO is a medium-term strategy; noticeable movement typically appears within 3–6 months, with technical fixes often yielding faster early results.

jsmPortal.q: What is a JSM Customer Portal?
jsmPortal.a: It is the self-service interface for Jira Service Management where customers or internal employees submit tickets, track status updates, and access help resources without needing full Jira licenses.

jsmPortal.q: Can we establish separate portals for distinct departments (IT, HR, Facilities)?
jsmPortal.a: Yes — we set up distinct request types, queues, and permissions per team, providing each department with its dedicated workspace within a single JSM instance.

jsmPortal.q: Do you configure Service Level Agreements (SLAs)?
jsmPortal.a: Yes — we define SLA metrics based on request types and priority levels, incorporating automated escalations and reporting to prevent unhandled tickets.

jsmPortal.q: Can the portal deflect routine requests using a knowledge base?
jsmPortal.a: Yes — we integrate searchable knowledge bases (such as Confluence) into the portal, allowing users to find self-service answers before submitting tickets.

jsmPortal.q: How long does a JSM Portal setup take?
jsmPortal.a: A standard implementation — portal styling, request types, SLA policies, and knowledge base integration — typically takes 1–3 weeks depending on organizational scope.

clickup.q: Do you configure ClickUp from scratch or reorganize existing workspaces?
clickup.a: Both. We construct clean ClickUp architectures from zero or audit and restructure existing workspaces that have grown disorganized over time.

clickup.q: Can ClickUp integrate with our existing tool stack?
clickup.a: Yes — we establish integrations with Slack, GitHub, Google Drive, and other platforms using native connectors or automated Zapier flows.

clickup.q: Will our team receive training on the new workspace structure?
clickup.a: Every implementation includes onboarding sessions and documentation to ensure your team adapts quickly to the new Spaces, workflows, and automations.

clickup.q: Can repetitive task management be automated in ClickUp?
clickup.a: Yes — we implement automations for status shifts, task assignments, due-date notifications, and recurring items to reduce manual administration.

clickup.q: What is the typical timeframe for a ClickUp workspace setup?
clickup.a: A standard workspace implementation takes 1–2 weeks, depending on team structures, workflow complexity, and third-party integrations.

support.q: What does an SLA support agreement cover?
support.a: Guaranteed response times scaled by incident severity (critical, high, standard), 24/7 uptime monitoring, bug remediation, and direct communication channels.

support.q: What is the response time for critical incidents?
support.a: Critical disruptions (service outages, data security risks) trigger immediate responses defined in your SLA — typically under 1 hour — prioritizing resolution over routine tasks.

support.q: Does support cover new feature additions alongside bug fixes?
support.a: Yes — support retainers cover ongoing bug fixes and system monitoring by default, with dedicated monthly developer hours allocatable toward new feature development.

support.q: Can you manage applications original built by other engineering teams?
support.a: Yes — we conduct an initial codebase and infrastructure audit to understand system architecture before taking over ongoing maintenance and development.

support.q: How are issue reports and feature requests submitted?
support.a: All requests are tracked and prioritized via dedicated communication channels — typically integrated directly into Slack or Jira Service Management.

analytics.q: Do you handle complete Google Analytics 4 (GA4) setups?
analytics.a: Yes — we set up GA4 instances (or migrate legacy implementations), configure conversion tracking, and integrate Google Tag Manager for reliable data collection.

analytics.q: Can specific user interactions be tracked?
analytics.a: Yes — we configure custom event tracking for critical interactions such as contact form submissions, dynamic link clicks, downloads, and checkout funnels.
Yes — we construct real-time visual dashboards accessible anytime, alongside providing periodic executive summaries outlining key traffic and conversion trends.

analytics.q: Do you assist with data analysis and optimization suggestions?
analytics.a: Yes — beyond setting up tracking systems, we interpret user behavior trends and provide actionable suggestions to improve conversion paths and site UX.

analytics.q: Is the analytics setup compliant with privacy regulations like GDPR?
analytics.a: Yes — we implement consent-aware tracking configurations integrated with cookie management banners to ensure compliance with international privacy laws.

infra.q: Which cloud platforms do you support (AWS, GCP, Azure)?
infra.a: We work with AWS, Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure — selecting or optimizing the provider that fits your architectural requirements and budget.

infra.q: Do you support self-hosted or on-premise infrastructure?
infra.a: Yes — alongside cloud environments, we manage dedicated servers and virtual private servers (VPS), including Linux server administration and web server setups (Nginx, Apache).

infra.q: How are system security and data backups handled?
infra.a: We implement access control policies, network firewalls, server hardening protocols, and automated daily backup routines with verified restoration testing.

infra.q: Can you audit infrastructure to lower monthly cloud costs?
infra.a: Yes — we analyze resource utilization, decommission idle assets, and configure auto-scaling rules to optimize compute spend, regularly reducing cloud infrastructure bills.

infra.q: Is ongoing operational support available after initial infrastructure setup?
infra.a: Yes — we offer ongoing infrastructure management, security patching, monitoring, and on-call support to keep systems stable as traffic grows.

devops.q: Do you build new CI/CD pipelines or optimize existing configurations?
devops.a: Both. We build continuous delivery pipelines from scratch or refine existing GitHub Actions or GitLab CI workflows to accelerate build speeds and deployment stability.

devops.q: Do deployment updates cause application downtime?
devops.a: No — we implement zero-downtime deployment strategies (such as rolling updates, blue-green deployments, or canary releases) to ensure continuous uptime.

devops.q: What safeguard happens if a deployment build fails?
devops.a: Automated rollbacks trigger immediately — if health checks detect failures post-deployment, the environment reverts automatically to the last stable release state.

devops.q: Is application monitoring and alert management included?
devops.a: Yes — we set up monitoring platforms (e.g., Datadog, Grafana) with automated alerts routed to Slack or email channels to identify issues before end-users do.

devops.q: How long does implementing a full DevOps pipeline take?
devops.a: A standard CI/CD pipeline covering build, test, deployment automation, and basic monitoring is typically established within 2–3 weeks.

web.q: When do you use React versus WordPress for web development?
web.a: React (Next.js) is chosen for complex, highly interactive web apps and custom SaaS portals. WordPress is ideal for marketing websites, blogs, and content-managed portals.

web.q: How do we determine which web framework best fits our project?
web.a: If your project requires complex data management, integrations, or custom user dashboards, React is ideal. If your primary need is marketing content managed by non-technical staff, WordPress is faster and cost-effective.

web.q: Is it possible to migrate from WordPress to React later?
web.a: Yes — many businesses start with a WordPress site and transition to a custom React web application as feature demands grow. We structure content architecture with scalable growth paths in mind.

web.q: Do you build custom e-commerce web applications?
web.a: Yes — we build WooCommerce platforms on WordPress for standard e-commerce stores, or custom React storefronts when high scale, bespoke checkout flows, and specialized performance are required.

web.q: What is the typical timeline for building a website or web app?
web.a: A standard WordPress website usually launches within 2–4 weeks. Custom React application development typically ranges from 6–12 weeks depending on scope and integrations.

web.q: Are your web applications compliant with European data privacy standards (GDPR)?
web.a: Yes — all web applications are engineered according to GDPR guidelines by default, including HTTPS encryption, secure authentication handling, and cookie consent mechanisms.

mobile.q: Why do you build mobile applications using Flutter?
mobile.a: Flutter allows us to write a unified codebase that compiles to native iOS and Android apps, delivering native performance and UI capabilities while cutting multi-platform development costs in half.

mobile.q: What is the delivery timeline for a mobile app project?
mobile.a: Most MVP-stage mobile applications launch in 6–10 weeks depending on feature scope and backend complexity. Concrete timelines are established during initial planning.

mobile.q: Does a cross-platform app look and feel native on both iOS and Android?
mobile.a: Yes — Flutter renders native UI components on both platforms, ensuring consistent branding alongside native platform navigation standards.

mobile.q: Do you manage publication to the Apple App Store and Google Play Store?
mobile.a: Yes — we handle the entire submission process including developer setup, app listings, screenshots, privacy policies, and store review requirements.

mobile.q: What post-launch support is available for mobile apps?
mobile.a: We provide ongoing app maintenance including bug fixes, mobile OS updates, analytics integration, and iterative feature development as your product scales.
